title: Match the Numeral to the Group

steps.body: Matching runs both directions: from a group, count and pick its numeral; from a numeral, read and find its group.
steps.narration: Matching runs both directions: from a group, count and pick its numeral; from a numeral, read and find its group.

widget.prompt: The card shows 6. Build the group it names.

commonCounts.feedback: Five leaves the promise unmet; the card's 6 asks for one more.
Seven breaks the promise upward; 6 refuses any extras.

widget.missFeedback: Read the card, build exactly that count.
widget.successFeedback: Six — numeral and group agree exactly, which is what matching means.

predict.prompt: The card says 7 and the group holds 6. A match?
predict.reveal: Numerals are exact promises; one missing thing breaks the match.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw match numeral.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw match numeral.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: A group shows 3 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: 4 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 3.
2 promises fewer dots than the group holds; the count reaches 3.
5 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 3.
Correct — the numeral 3 is the written name for a group of exactly 3.

widget.prompt: Look at the ten-frame flash and choose the matching numeral.

commonPicks.feedback: 3 misses 1 of the visible dots. Group the dots, then count the full group as 4.
5 counts 1 extra. Touch each dot once in your mind — the group holds 4.

widget.missFeedback: Watch again and group the ten-frame: it shows 4 dots.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 4! The ten-frame and numeral agree.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 8? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 8 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 9.
10 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 8 lands on 9.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 8: you land on 9.
widget.successFeedback: 9 — the next numeral in the writing order is the next number in the song.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 9.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 8 means one hop, stopping on 9.
